name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_STATEMENTBASEDMULTI_Q01 - Testicular lobule compartments tubules and interstitial cells

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V):

Statement I: The scrotum maintains the temperature of the testes 2 to 2.5°C lower than the normal internal body temperature.

Statement II: Each adult human testis has approximately 250 compartments called testicular lobules.

Statement III: Each testicular lobule contains one to three highly coiled seminiferous tubules in which sperms are produced.

Statement IV: The male germ cells lining the seminiferous tubules undergo meiotic divisions leading to sperm formation.

Statement V: Sertoli cells line the interior of the seminiferous tubules and provide nutrition to the germ cells.

Which of the following options represents the correct evaluation of the statements?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of scrotal thermoregulatory function
The scrotum houses the testes outside the abdominal cavity to maintain a local temperature 2 to 2.5°C lower than core body temperature, ensuring optimal conditions for spermatogenesis.

Step 2: Evaluation of testicular lobular organization
Fibrous septa internally subdivide each adult human testis into approximately 250 compartments known as testicular lobules.

Step 3: Evaluation of seminiferous tubule frequency per lobule
Within each testicular lobule, one to three highly convoluted seminiferous tubules reside, serving as the actual functional sites of sperm generation.

Step 4: Evaluation of spermatogenic germ cell meiosis
Male germ cells (spermatogonia) lining the basement membrane of seminiferous tubules undergo meiotic reduction divisions to produce haploid spermatozoa.

Step 5: Evaluation of Sertoli cell trophic support
Interspersed columnar Sertoli cells directly envelop developing spermatogenic cells and furnish vital metabolic nutrition.

Step 6: Conceptual conclusion
All five statements are correct because scrotal thermoregulation, lobular partitioning, tubular density, germ cell meiosis, and Sertoli nutritional support accurately reflect male reproductive anatomy and physiology.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, IV, and V are all correct
Statements I, II, and III only are correct
Statements I, III, IV, and V only are correct
Statements II, IV, and V only are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_STATEMENTBASEDMULTI_Q02 - Ovarian dimensions female accessory ducts and uterine wall

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V):

Statement I: Each ovary is about 2 to 4 cm in length and is connected to the pelvic wall and uterus by ligaments.

Statement II: The oviducts, uterus, and vagina constitute the female accessory ducts.

Statement III: The edges of the funnel-shaped infundibulum possess finger-like projections called fimbriae that help collect the ovum.

Statement IV: The cervical canal along with the vagina forms the birth canal.

Statement V: The myometrium is the inner glandular layer of the uterus that undergoes cyclical changes during the menstrual cycle.

Which of the following options represents the correct evaluation of the statements?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of ovarian dimensions and ligaments
Each human ovary measures 2 to 4 cm in length and is held in position within the pelvic cavity by peritoneal ligamentous folds connected to the pelvic wall and uterus.

Step 2: Evaluation of female accessory duct system
The female ductal pathway that conducts gametes and supports fetal passage comprises the paired fallopian tubes (oviducts), the single uterus, and the vagina.

Step 3: Evaluation of infundibular fimbriae role
The ovarian terminal opening of the oviduct expands as the funnel-shaped infundibulum, bordered by motile ciliated fimbriae that actively gather the ovulated oocyte.

Step 4: Evaluation of birth canal anatomy
The central lumen of the uterine cervix, designated as the cervical canal, unites with the vaginal canal to form the composite birth canal.

Step 5: Evaluation of uterine wall layer differentiation
The middle muscular layer is the myometrium, which contracts during labor; the inner glandular layer that lines the uterine cavity and exhibits cyclical modifications during menstruation is the endometrium.

Step 6: Conceptual conclusion
The claims regarding ovarian morphology, accessory ducts, fimbriae function, and the birth canal are correct, whereas the claim assigning endometrial cyclical changes to the muscular myometrium is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III only are correct
Statements I, II, III, and IV are correct, but Statement V is incorrect
Statements I, II, III, IV, and V are all correct
Statements II, III, and V are correct, but Statements I and IV are incorrect

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_STATEMENTBASEDMULTI_Q03 - Endocrine regulation of spermatogenesis and sperm ejaculate characteristics

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V):

Statement I: Spermatogenesis starts at puberty due to a significant increase in the secretion of hypothalamic gonadotropin releasing hormone.

Statement II: Luteinizing hormone acts at the Leydig cells and stimulates the synthesis and secretion of androgens.

Statement III: Follicle stimulating hormone acts on the Sertoli cells and stimulates secretion of factors that help in spermiogenesis.

Statement IV: A human male ejaculates about 200 to 300 million sperms during a single coitus.

Statement V: The middle piece of the sperm contains an enzyme-filled cap called acrosome that dissolves egg membranes.

Which of the following options represents the correct evaluation of the statements?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of hypothalamic GnRH stimulation at puberty
Pubertal onset of male gametogenesis is triggered by heightened pulsatile release of hypothalamic gonadotropin releasing hormone.

Step 2: Evaluation of LH stimulation on interstitial cells
Anterior pituitary LH targets Leydig cells in the interstitial tissue, stimulating androgen biosynthesis to sustain spermatogenesis.

Step 3: Evaluation of FSH action on Sertoli cells
Anterior pituitary FSH binds Sertoli cell receptors, inducing the release of biochemical factors that facilitate spermiogenic transformation of spermatids into spermatozoa.

Step 4: Evaluation of normal human ejaculate volume and sperm count
A typical human male ejaculation releases 200 to 300 million spermatozoa, with healthy fertility demanding normal morphology and vigorous motility.

Step 5: Evaluation of sperm anatomical compartmentalization
The acrosome is an enzyme-rich cap derived from the Golgi apparatus covering the anterior sperm nucleus in the head; the middle piece contains densely packed mitochondria that furnish motility energy.

Step 6: Conceptual conclusion
The hormonal cascade of GnRH, LH, and FSH alongside ejaculate numbers are correctly described, whereas the claim locating the hydrolytic acrosome in the mitochondrial middle piece is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III only are correct
Statements I, II, III, IV, and V are all correct
Statements I, II, III, and IV are correct, but Statement V is incorrect
Statements II, IV, and V only are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_STATEMENTBASEDMULTI_Q04 - Oogonial reserve primary follicle count and tertiary antrum

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V):

Statement I: Oogenesis is initiated during fetal life, and no more oogonia are formed and added after birth.

Statement II: Primary oocytes start division and get temporarily arrested at prophase-I of the meiotic division.

Statement III: Due to extensive follicular degeneration from birth to puberty, only 60,000 to 80,000 primary follicles remain in each ovary at puberty.

Statement IV: The tertiary follicle is characterized by the formation of a distinct fluid-filled cavity called the antrum.

Statement V: The first meiotic division of the primary oocyte produces two equal haploid daughter cells that share cytoplasm evenly.

Which of the following options represents the correct evaluation of the statements?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of prenatal oogonial formation
Female germ cells proliferate strictly during embryonic development, generating all oogonia before birth with zero additions during postnatal life.

Step 2: Evaluation of meiotic arrest in primary oocytes
Developing primary oocytes enter meiosis I during fetal gestation and undergo prolonged developmental arrest at prophase-I.

Step 3: Evaluation of follicular atresia and pubertal count
Widespread atresia between infancy and puberty reduces the initial ovarian follicle population down to roughly 60,000 to 80,000 viable primary follicles per ovary.

Step 4: Evaluation of tertiary follicle antrum formation
Transition from secondary to tertiary follicle is marked by fluid accumulation creating an internal cavity named the antrum.

Step 5: Evaluation of cytokinesis symmetry during meiosis I
Meiosis I in oogenesis is distinctly asymmetrical, generating a large nutrient-laden secondary oocyte and a minuscule first polar body, rather than equal daughter cells.

Step 6: Conceptual conclusion
The facts regarding fetal oogonial limits, meiotic arrest, pubertal follicle numbers, and tertiary antrum development are correct, whereas claiming meiosis I yields equal cytoplasmic division is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, and V are correct, but Statement IV is incorrect
Statements II, III, and IV only are correct
Statements I, III, and IV only are correct
Statements I, II, III, and IV are correct, but Statement V is incorrect

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_STATEMENTBASEDMULTI_Q05 - Endometrial breakdown gonadotropin surge and corpus luteum regression

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V):

Statement I: Menstrual flow results due to the breakdown of the endometrial lining of the uterus and its blood vessels.

Statement II: Secretion of LH and FSH increases gradually during the follicular phase and stimulates ovarian estrogen secretion.

Statement III: The mid-cycle LH surge induces the rupture of the mature Graafian follicle and releases the secondary oocyte.

Statement IV: The corpus luteum secretes large amounts of progesterone, which is essential for the maintenance of the endometrium.

Statement V: In the absence of fertilisation, high levels of human placental lactogen sustain the corpus luteum for several months.

Which of the following options represents the correct evaluation of the statements?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of menstrual shedding mechanism
Progesterone withdrawal at the conclusion of an infertile cycle triggers ischemia, necrosis, and sloughing of the functional endometrial mucosa and associated vasculature.

Step 2: Evaluation of gonadotropin and estrogen dynamics in the follicular phase
Gradual elevation of anterior pituitary LH and FSH stimulates follicular development and prompts granulosa thecal cells to produce rising quantities of estrogens.

Step 3: Evaluation of mid-cycle LH surge and ovulation
Mid-cycle positive feedback induces a precipitous spike in LH release (the LH surge), which directly causes rupture of the Graafian follicle to release the secondary oocyte.

Step 4: Evaluation of corpus luteum endocrine secretion
Remnants of the ovulated follicle reorganize into the vascularized corpus luteum, producing substantial progesterone to render the endometrium receptive for implantation.

Step 5: Evaluation of luteal fate in non-pregnant cycles
Without fertilisation, the corpus luteum degenerates into an inactive corpus albicans; human placental lactogen is a placental hormone of pregnancy that does not exist in non-conceptive menstrual cycles.

Step 6: Conceptual conclusion
The claims describing menstrual breakdown, follicular gonadotropin stimulation, ovulatory LH surge, and luteal progesterone secretion are correct, whereas the claim that human placental lactogen sustains the corpus luteum without fertilisation is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, and IV are correct, but Statement V is incorrect
Statements I, II, and III only are correct
Statements I, II, III, IV, and V are all correct
Statements II, III, and IV only are correct

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_HUMANREPRODUCTION_STATEMENTBASEDMULTI_Q06 - Polyspermy prevention meiotic resumption blastocyst and pregnancy hormones

questiontext.text:
Consider the following five statements (I, II, III, IV, and V):

Statement I: Contact of a sperm with the zona pellucida induces membrane modifications that block the entry of additional sperms.

Statement II: Sperm entry into the secondary oocyte induces the completion of its second meiotic division.

Statement III: In the blastocyst, the cells are arranged into an outer trophoblast and an inner group called the inner cell mass.

Statement IV: Human chorionic gonadotropin, human placental lactogen, and relaxin are produced in women only during pregnancy.

Statement V: The signals for parturition originate from the fully developed fetus and the placenta, triggering the foetal ejection reflex.

Which of the following options represents the correct evaluation of the statements?

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Evaluation of zona reaction blocking polyspermy
Initial sperm penetration through the zona pellucida triggers structural changes in the coat, establishing a permanent barrier against secondary sperm entry.

Step 2: Evaluation of meiotic resumption upon fertilisation
Sperm fusion releases the secondary oocyte from metaphase-II arrest, prompting an unequal second meiotic division that forms a second polar body and the mature ovum nucleus.

Step 3: Evaluation of blastocyst cellular architecture
The pre-implantation blastocyst organizes into a peripheral trophoblast dedicated to uterine invasion and placenta formation, and a pluripotent inner cell mass destined to form the embryo.

Step 4: Evaluation of gestation-specific hormone synthesis
Placental secretions of hCG and hPL together with late ovarian relaxin serve as physiological endocrine hallmarks restricted entirely to pregnant females.

Step 5: Evaluation of neuroendocrine parturition initiation
Terminal developmental maturity of the fetus and placenta generates hormonal signals that initiate mild uterine contractions, establishing the positive neuroendocrine foetal ejection reflex.

Step 6: Conceptual conclusion
All five statements are correct because the block to polyspermy, meiotic completion, blastocyst differentiation, pregnancy-specific hormones, and the foetal ejection reflex accurately delineate the reproductive and developmental sequence.

answer.text: Statements I, II, III, and IV only are correct
Statements I, II, III, IV, and V are all correct
Statements II, III, IV, and V only are correct
Statements I, III, and V only are correct
